$comment: Generated by bin/gen-lwmin.mjs from the reference (CONVENTIONS W3, ticket 0016); read by bin/workspace-minimum.mjs. Per routine: `args` are Fortran argument names (options as Fortran letters; SELECT is the number of leading .TRUE. entries), over the grid of bin/gen-lwkopt.mjs; each row ends with, per workspace of `workspaces`: its minimum and its effective minimum on zero data, the same on seeded random data, the same on that data made rank-deficient (every second column of each 2-D input a copy of the one before; null: that run crashed or was rejected), the length each was given while another was measured, and last the seed of the random data (bin/lib/fortran-ref.mjs fills the real and complex inputs, in argument order, with a Park-Miller sequence from it). A `check` minimum is the smallest length whose call does not return INFO = `info` (min - 1 is rejected); its effective minimum the smallest length at which no callee rejects what the routine passes it either and nothing past the length is written (null: callees reject even at the bound). `overruns`: per workspace, the rows where the reference writes past what its own check accepts (`own`: the minimum of that check, `wrote`: the last element written, in `example`); writes only, reads past the length are not seen. A `declared` minimum (and effective minimum) is the extent the reference declares. Only rows whose arguments the reference accepts are recorded. `unmeasured`: workspaces with no minimum, and why. `noInfo`: modules whose reference has no INFO argument, so rejects nothing. `noCheck`: modules whose reference never rejects any workspace length (value: the entry hash). `unhandled`: modules the generator cannot measure, and why (bin/lib/lwmin.mjs UNHANDLED).
